title: Qualifying & Disqualifying
summary: Who qualifies, every DQ reason, and exactly what to say when someone is disqualified.

blocks.html:
A consumer qualifies for the transfer when they:

  • Have Medicare Parts A and B
  • Have the red, white and blue card, or at least know their Medicare number or Social Security number (they never read or give it to you)
  • Have confirmed their state and ZIP
  • Do NOT have insurance through work, retirement, the VA or other military coverage, or a Native American tribe
  • Say yes to giving the specialist a few minutes
Medicaid is not on this list as a yes-or-no rule. A consumer with Medicaid and Medicare can qualify. A consumer without Medicaid can qualify too.

blocks.title: Qualify with the script, not your gut
blocks.html: Don't decide someone "sounds too young" or "probably doesn't qualify." Ask the questions. The answers decide.

blocks.question: Which consumer qualifies for the transfer?
choices: Has Parts A and B but still has insurance through their job
Has Parts A and B, the red, white and blue card, confirms ZIP, no work or VA insurance, and agrees to a few minutes
Has Parts A and B and Tricare for Life
Has only Medicaid and no Medicare
blocks.explanation: They must pass every question and give permission. Work insurance, no Medicare, and Tricare are all DQs.

blocks.html:
Code as DQ (Disqualified) when the consumer has:

  • No Medicare Parts A and B
  • Military coverage: VA, Tricare, Tricare for Life, or CHAMPVA
  • Insurance through work or retirement (employer, union, or retiree plans)
  • Coverage through a Native American tribe

blocks.title: No Medicare Parts A and B

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: No, I'm not on Medicare yet.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (Code as DQ)

blocks.title: Work, retirement, VA or other DQ coverage

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Yes, I've got Tricare for Life.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (CODE AS DQ)

blocks.title: DQ is not the same as Not Interested
blocks.html: A DQ means they can't qualify. Not Interested means they won't continue. Don't mix them up; miscoding patterns are an improper call handling issue.

blocks.question: Which is a DQ reason?
choices: Says they're busy
Receives Medicaid
Covered by a Native American tribe
Lost their red, white and blue card
blocks.explanation: Tribal coverage is a DQ. The others are not.

blocks.html: Real consumers don't use the words on the DQ list. They say it their own way. Read each answer and decide.

blocks.question: You ask about work or VA insurance. The consumer says, "I've got Tricare for Life." What now?
choices: Code as Not Interested
Continue to the transfer ask; Tricare for Life is just Medicare
Rebut with "I understand, but MANY people are finding out RIGHT now..."
Read "Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day." and code DQ
blocks.explanation: Tricare for Life is military coverage, which is a DQ.

blocks.question: The consumer says, "Just the insurance from my retirement plan with the city." What now?
choices: Retirement plans don't count; continue
It is insurance through retirement, so read the mistake line and code DQ
Schedule a callback
Ask them to cancel the retirement plan first
blocks.explanation: Insurance through work or retirement is a DQ.

blocks.question: At the double-confirm, the consumer says, "I just have the Medicaid card." What do you say?
choices: Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Okay, no problem, but you DO have your Medicare number, correct?
blocks.explanation: That is the "I have ____ card" branch. Ask if they have their Medicare number. If yes, continue; if no, read the No line.

blocks.question: The consumer says, "I have Medicaid, and yes, I have Medicare A and B too." What now?
choices: Code DQ because they have Medicaid
Keep going; Medicaid is not a DQ
Ask them to pick one
Code DNC

blocks.question: The consumer says, "I get my health insurance through my wife's job." What now?
choices: Continue, because it's not their own job
Rebut and ask for the transfer
Code as Wrong Number
Treat it as insurance through work: read the mistake line and code DQ
blocks.explanation: Coverage through an employer plan is insurance through work. That is a DQ.

blocks.question: The consumer says, "I use CHAMPVA." What now?
choices: Continue; CHAMPVA isn't the VA
DQ; CHAMPVA is military coverage
Transfer and let the specialist decide
Code Not Interested
blocks.explanation: CHAMPVA is on the military coverage DQ list.

blocks.html: Consumers almost never say "I have insurance through my employer." They say it sideways, often before or after you ask the work or VA question. You have to hear it, and when you do, read the DQ line.

blocks.title: What to listen for
blocks.html:
1. Retiree coverage: "a plan through my old job", "my retirement", "my pension", "the city", "the union". This includes retiree Medicare Advantage plans through a former employer.
  2. VA or Tricare: VA, Tricare, Tricare for Life, CHAMPVA.
  3. Employer coverage: through their job or a spouse's job.
  4. No Medicare A and B: only Part A, only Medicaid, not on Medicare yet.

blocks.title: How it sounds when they say it sideways

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I've got the plan through the city, from when I retired.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Retiree coverage. DQ.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: My Advantage plan comes through the union.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Retiree coverage, even though it's Medicare Advantage. DQ.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: My husband still works, so I'm on his insurance.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Employer coverage through a spouse. DQ.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I go to the VA for everything.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: VA. DQ.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I only have Part A. I never signed up for B.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: No Medicare A and B. DQ.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I have Medicaid through the state.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: NOT a DQ. Medicaid is fine. Keep going.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Insurance through work, retirement or the VA:

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Code as DQ. No Medicare A and B:

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Code as DQ. Don't rebut a DQ, and don't transfer it to be "safe."

blocks.title: When in doubt, ask one clarifying question
blocks.html:
If you're not sure where the coverage comes from, ask: "Is that through a job or retirement?"

This is a Compliance Model habit. One short question, then wait. If it's through a job, retirement, a union or the military, read the DQ line. If not, keep going.

blocks.title: What the model agents actually say

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I don't have insurance with the VA, but I have Kaiser.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The Compliance Model splits the question so nothing gets missed:

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, all right, no problem. And do you have insurance through a job?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: What? Now?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The Pace Model puts it in plain words for a confused consumer:

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Work, like an old job, or the VA military?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I have public aid.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: The Pace Model clarifies instead of assuming:

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay. Through Medicaid, not Medicare?

blocks.question: You ask the work or VA question. The consumer says, "No, but my Medicare Advantage plan is through my old company's retirement." What now?
choices: They said no, so continue to the transfer ask
Medicare Advantage is fine, so continue
Read "Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day." and code DQ
Rebut with the not interested line
blocks.explanation: A retiree plan through a former employer is insurance through retirement, even if it's Medicare Advantage.

blocks.question: The consumer says, "I've got my pension plan coverage." You aren't sure if that's health insurance. What do you do?
choices: Assume it isn't and transfer
Ask one clarifying question: "Is that through a job or retirement?"
Code DQ without asking
Tell them the specialist will figure it out
blocks.explanation: When in doubt, ask one short clarifying question and wait for the answer.

blocks.question: Which answer is NOT a DQ?
choices: "I use Tricare for Life."
"I'm on my wife's plan from her job."
"I get Medicaid along with my Medicare."
"I only have Part A."
blocks.explanation: Medicaid with Medicare continues. Tricare, employer coverage and no Part B are all DQs.

questions.question: Which of these is a DQ reason?
choices: Not knowing what Parts A and B are
Being busy
Insurance through work or retirement
Receiving Medicaid
questions.explanation: Work or retirement insurance is a DQ.

questions.question: Which military coverages are DQs?
choices: VA, Tricare, Tricare for Life and CHAMPVA
Only Tricare
None; military coverage is fine
Only the VA
questions.explanation: All four military coverages are DQs.

questions.question: A consumer says they are covered by their tribe. How do you code it?
choices: DQ
No English
Not Interested
Transfer
questions.explanation: Coverage by a Native American tribe is a DQ.

questions.question: What line do you read when a consumer says Yes to work or VA insurance?
choices: I understand, but MANY people are finding out RIGHT now that they ACTUALLY qualify for WAY more than they're receiving.
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
No problem, I'll add you to our internal do not call list immediately and you won't receive any further calls from our company. We do apologize for any inconvenience, have a great day.
questions.explanation: Read "Oh, there must have been a mistake..." and code DQ.

questions.question: A consumer has Medicaid and Medicare Parts A and B. Can they qualify?
choices: Only on a callback
No, Medicaid is a DQ
Only if they drop Medicaid
Yes, Medicaid is not a DQ
questions.explanation: Medicaid yes or no both continue.

questions.question: A consumer says, "I'm 62 and not on Medicare yet." What happens?
choices: Transfer them anyway
Schedule a callback for when they turn 65
Code Not Interested
DQ; they don't have Medicare Parts A and B
questions.explanation: No Medicare Parts A and B is a DQ.

questions.question: What is the difference between DQ and Not Interested?
choices: NI is only used after a transfer
They mean the same thing
DQ is for rude people; NI is for polite people
DQ means they can't qualify; Not Interested means they won't continue
questions.explanation: Keep them straight. Miscoding is improper call handling.

questions.question: A consumer says, "My old union plan still covers me." What now?
choices: Rebut with the busy rebuttal
Continue; unions don't count
DQ; that is insurance through work or retirement
Code DNC
questions.explanation: Union and retiree plans are work/retirement insurance.

questions.question: Why does the script double-confirm the red, white and blue card?
choices: To confirm their address
To be sure the consumer really has Medicare Parts A and B
To collect their card number
To check their Medicaid balance
questions.explanation: Double-confirming Parts A and B is a compliance step. You don't collect the number.

questions.question: Before you ask, a consumer says, "I only have Tricare for Life, is that okay?" What do you do?
choices: Tell them it's fine and keep going
Put them on hold
Read the mistake line and code DQ
Use the "I've already got it" rebuttal
questions.explanation: Tricare for Life is a DQ no matter when in the call it comes up.

questions.question: The consumer says, "I have a plan through the union from when I retired." What now?
choices: Continue; union plans don't count
Read "Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day." and code DQ
Rebut and transfer
Code Not Interested
questions.explanation: Retiree coverage through a union is insurance through retirement. Read the DQ line.

questions.question: The consumer says, "I get my care at the VA, but I have Medicare too." What now?
choices: Continue, since they have Medicare
Ask about the red, white and blue card
DQ: VA coverage. Read the mistake line and code DQ
Transfer and let the specialist decide
questions.explanation: VA and Tricare coverage are DQs even with Medicare.
